providers.name: Plovdiv State Archives
providers.what: A branch of the State Agency «Архиви»; archive id 16 in the agency's digital archive, so it can be searched on its own. Its own slice of the digital archive answered a search for «снимка» with 153 items. All of Bulgaria's state archives are branches of one body, the State Agency «Архиви», on one site, and the terms are the same for all of them. The free DIGITAL ARCHIVE («ДИГИТАЛЕН АРХИВ») searches each archive separately and returns described items with a full citation — archive > fond > опис > архивна единица > лист — and the image with them. It is a SELECTION, in the hundreds per archive, not a bulk scan of registers. Fond lists and finding aids are published per archive. THE REGISTERS ARE MOSTLY NOT HERE, AND THE REASON IS A LAW: civil registration began on 1 January 1893, the municipality writes the registers and KEEPS THEM FOR 130 YEARS before transferring them to the state archive, so until that term runs out certified copies come from the municipality of birth or residence, not from the archive. Two more doors the agency names itself: it CANNOT certify Bulgarian origin — that is the Executive Agency for Bulgarians Abroad, with citizenship at the Ministry of Justice — and service in the Bulgarian army is checked only by the Държавен военноисторически архив at Veliko Tarnovo.
providers.triageNote: Surveyed 2026-10-09; one survey covers all 28 agency archives, which share a site and a policy. www.archives.government.bg opens with no account asked for. Its ДИГИТАЛЕН АРХИВ form posts to /search.php with an archive id, and a keyword search returns «Показани резултати: N» with thumbnails under /illustrations/ and the citation path «фонд > опис > а.е. > лист»; «Пловдив» in archive 16 returned 86. Each archive page carries Фондове, Фондообразуватели, Архивни справочници, Пътеводители, Списък на фондове and Уникални и особено ценни документи. The «Услуги и използване» page states the 130-year rule: «Актовете по гражданско състояние … се съставят от общината … и се съхраняват в нея 130 години, след което се предават в съответния държавен архив, съгласно чл. 85, ал. 3 от Закона за гражданската регистрация», and that until then «заверени преписи и копия се издават от съответната община». NOT REACHED: the agency documents free access to the digitised Exarchate parish registers «чрез Информационната система на държавните архиви (ИСДА) на адрес: http://isda.archives.government.bg:84/FundSearch.aspx» — isda.archives.government.bg resolves to 212.122.187.196 and timed out on ports 84, 8081, 80 and 443, over http and https, to curl and to a real browser. The same address is behind the site's «Е-УСЛУГИ» link. Recorded as unreachable from here, not as closed. This archive is id 16 in the /search.php «tdaa» list.

providers.what: A branch of the State Agency «Архиви»; archive id 4 in the agency's digital archive, so it can be searched on its own. All of Bulgaria's state archives are branches of one body, the State Agency «Архиви», on one site, and the terms are the same for all of them. The free DIGITAL ARCHIVE («ДИГИТАЛЕН АРХИВ») searches each archive separately and returns described items with a full citation — archive > fond > опис > архивна единица > лист — and the image with them. It is a SELECTION, in the hundreds per archive, not a bulk scan of registers. Fond lists and finding aids are published per archive. THE REGISTERS ARE MOSTLY NOT HERE, AND THE REASON IS A LAW: civil registration began on 1 January 1893, the municipality writes the registers and KEEPS THEM FOR 130 YEARS before transferring them to the state archive, so until that term runs out certified copies come from the municipality of birth or residence, not from the archive. Two more doors the agency names itself: it CANNOT certify Bulgarian origin — that is the Executive Agency for Bulgarians Abroad, with citizenship at the Ministry of Justice — and service in the Bulgarian army is checked only by the Държавен военноисторически архив at Veliko Tarnovo.
providers.triageNote: Surveyed 2026-10-09; one survey covers all 28 agency archives, which share a site and a policy. www.archives.government.bg opens with no account asked for. Its ДИГИТАЛЕН АРХИВ form posts to /search.php with an archive id, and a keyword search returns «Показани резултати: N» with thumbnails under /illustrations/ and the citation path «фонд > опис > а.е. > лист»; «Пловдив» in archive 16 returned 86. Each archive page carries Фондове, Фондообразуватели, Архивни справочници, Пътеводители, Списък на фондове and Уникални и особено ценни документи. The «Услуги и използване» page states the 130-year rule: «Актовете по гражданско състояние … се съставят от общината … и се съхраняват в нея 130 години, след което се предават в съответния държавен архив, съгласно чл. 85, ал. 3 от Закона за гражданската регистрация», and that until then «заверени преписи и копия се издават от съответната община». NOT REACHED: the agency documents free access to the digitised Exarchate parish registers «чрез Информационната система на държавните архиви (ИСДА) на адрес: http://isda.archives.government.bg:84/FundSearch.aspx» — isda.archives.government.bg resolves to 212.122.187.196 and timed out on ports 84, 8081, 80 and 443, over http and https, to curl and to a real browser. The same address is behind the site's «Е-УСЛУГИ» link. Recorded as unreachable from here, not as closed. This archive is id 4 in the /search.php «tdaa» list.

providers.name: BillionGraves
providers.what: GPS-tagged headstone photographs. Smaller than Find a Grave but its coordinates are per-stone, which Find a Grave's often are not. FREE AND PAID ARE SPLIT DOWN THE MIDDLE, surveyed 7 October 2026 at a South African cemetery: the search, the transcription — name with full birth and death dates — and the per-stone GPS coordinates are free and need no account, and so is a 180x135 thumbnail of the stone. THE FULL-RESOLUTION PHOTOGRAPH IS NOT: it requires an account and a subscription. The thumbnail is far too small to read an inscription, so a transcription taken from here CANNOT BE CHECKED AGAINST THE STONE without paying — which matters, because a volunteer's reading of a weathered date is exactly the thing an archive will want to verify. AND ITS SEARCH URL SILENTLY IGNORES WHAT YOU ASK IT, which makes it USABLE FOR A POSITIVE AND USELESS FOR A NEGATIVE: a hit here is a hit, and no absence may be quoted from it. Verified 9 October: `cemetery_country=United+Kingdom` is accepted and disregarded — the results still carry United States and Australian stones — and `page` does nothing at all, `page=7` returning the identical six records as `page=1` under a footer reading «Page 1 of 178». The footer asserts a depth the URL cannot reach, so the first page is not the result set and nothing that looks like «no match in that country» is one.
providers.triageNote:
THE SECOND CORRECTION IN AN HOUR, AND THE REASON THE ROW SAYS WHAT IT SAYS. Another session of this project retested BillionGraves on 9 October after it had been written off as blocked, found it answers a browser at once, and published «25 burials, none in the United Kingdom» with a SMITH control «filtered to the United Kingdom». Both halves were wrong: at `size=50` four Sanigars appear in England — three at Holy Trinity, Kingswood and one at Scartho Road, Grimsby — and the control was never filtered at all, because the country parameter is ignored.

VERIFIED HERE 9 October, independently, because a measurement that has already been corrected once should not be taken on trust: with `cemetery_country=United+Kingdom` the result set still contains United States and Australian stones; `page=7` and `page=1` return the same six names and the same «Page 1 of 178» footer. Not verified here: that about ten thousand records exist behind that footer, which is that session's count.

The useful shape of it: the site is open, the transcriptions are free, and the URL is a window onto the first page only. Drive its own interface before concluding anything is not there.

providers.name: Catholic Metropolitan Cemeteries Trust — Brisbane (cemsearch)
providers.what: The burial register search for the Roman Catholic cemeteries of the Archdiocese of Brisbane, Nudgee among them — NINE cemeteries. Returns register number, cemetery, name, birth, death, interment date and PLOT NUMBER. It is NOT in the Brisbane City Council grave search, because these are not council cemeteries: a family buried here is invisible to the council portal and to the aggregators that copy it. Queried by POST to `query.php?type=Deceased` with `CemeteryCode=%` and `SectionCode=%` — passing «All» returns nothing. Used from the Falco family archive, where it produced five burials that corrected two death dates carried from a family tree.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Falco family archive, which has used it repeatedly. Access class still needs a person: it answers without a login, but nobody has surveyed what an ordinary visitor is charged for a full register entry, so it stays unsurveyed. No Wikidata id established for the operating trust and none was guessed.

providers.name: Bristol Archives
providers.what: The city record office for Bristol: Church of England parish registers for the Bristol parishes, plus the city's own papers. The registers themselves are NOT online here — they are filmed on Ancestry, behind a subscription. What this office does do is read an entry for you: a seven-part enquiry about one 1828 marriage register entry was answered in nine days, in full, FREE, by staff who had viewed the record. Their quoted research service is £13 for up to half an hour and was not charged. The reply also corrected a surname spelling that two index sites had both transcribed the same way, and volunteered a later record that had not been asked about. Worth writing to.
providers.triageNote: Added from the D'Arcy archive after a free lookup answered in nine days. access=onsite: the paper is in the building and the films are on a commercial site.

providers.name: Bundesarchiv
providers.what: The German Federal Archives. Civil and military administration of the Prussian provinces, the wartime records, and the card indexes of the expelled — much of it for ground that is no longer German.

providers.name: CEMLA — Centro de Estudios Migratorios Latinoamericanos
providers.what: Buenos Aires port arrival books, 1882–1960, indexed by passenger name. Worked by the Blažević archive across four spellings of the same surname — which is how it has to be worked, because the clerk wrote what he heard. Not yet surveyed. NO SEAT RECORDED, DELIBERATELY. This is the one row the source-layer audit's `at` finding genuinely applies to — every other row it named is a COUNTRYWIDE kind, which sourcesNear() exempts from distance sorting, so a missing seat costs them nothing. CEMLA is filed as an index and is sorted by distance, and it does sink. Its Wikidata item (Q140429797) states a country, a founding year and a website and NO coordinates, so there is nothing to write: the institute is in Buenos Aires by its own description, which is prose and not a claim, and a coordinate inferred from prose is the guess this project refuses.
providers.triageNote: Added from the family research archives, which record work actually done here. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Chronicling America
providers.what: The Library of Congress's digitised American newspapers, full-text and free.

providers.name: Corsica Genealogie (RHFC)
providers.what: A volunteer register index covering 226 Corsican communes. Worked by the Defranceski archive against the Corsican records. Not yet surveyed.
providers.triageNote: Added from the family research archives, which record work actually done here. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Pazinu
providers.what: The Pazin State Archive, which holds the parish registers of central Istria. They will search, certify and post a named record for a fee. Its registers are also filmed as the ZM34K series, supplied as page images. Two of those reels were mapped frame by frame on 30 September 2026 and their contents recorded, because the archive's own paper inventory proved unreliable for them: ZM34K-214 and ZM34K-215 together run M01068774-M01070236 (1,463 contiguous frames) and hold THIRTEEN books - Cerovlje status animarum XIX-XX c.; Gologorica baptisms 1764-1788, 1770-1781, 1784-1880 and 1940-1948, deaths 1646-1806 and 1784-1880, marriages 1770-1789, and status animarum for 1826, 1862, 1894 and 1921; and Gracisce baptisms 1667-1745 with confirmations 1690-1694, and baptisms 1746-1840. TWO TRAPS. The paper inventory's section headings file both Gracisce books under a GOLOGORICA heading, and it stops the Gracisce baptisms at 1780 when the film's own title card says 1840. LINDAR IS NOT ON THESE TWO REELS - it is on ZM34K-219 and 220. Each book is preceded by a printed title card naming the zupa, the register and the years; that card, not the inventory, is the authority. WALKED SO FAR, so the next reader need not repeat it: on ZM34K-214 the GOLOGORICA DEATH REGISTER 1784-1880 is read ENTRY BY ENTRY end to end - M01069226-M01069297 (cover, flyleaf and pages 1-135, 96 years), plus its alphabetical INDEX at M01069299-M01069313, with M01069314 the film's own KRAJ / END OF ITEM target. Three things about that book are worth knowing before opening it. (1) Its index is a HOUSEHOLD directory, not a name list: each block is a surname, a byname, a HOUSE NUMBER and then the household's dead with the page each is on - and a married woman is entered under her HUSBAND'S surname, so a name search of the index will miss her. (2) The index ends with a column headed Extranei listing the people who died in the parish and did not belong to it, each with the place they came from - a ready-made list of where this parish's incomers originated, naming Krbune, Cerovlje and Friuli. (3) The index sometimes carries detail the register entry itself omits, so it is a second witness and not only a finding aid. The film also DUPLICATES some openings, and twice the duplicate exposure was the only readable one. Frame numbering of the other twelve books on these reels is in the 30 September mapping above. ALSO WALKED on ZM34K-214: the GOLOGORICA STATUS ANIMARUM of 1826 (M01069315-M01069435), and in particular its printed column 'Locus ex quo vel ad quem' - whence, or whither - read across every opening. That column is the most useful thing on either reel for anyone tracing movement in central Istria: for each household it names the PARISH a person came from or went to, THE HOUSE NUMBER AT THE FAR END, and the year. Counting it out for Gologorica gives Gracisce 16, Paz 9, Novaki 8, Krbune 6, Gradinje 6, Pazin 4, Cerovlje 3, DragUc 3, Lindar 2, Dol 2, Zminj 1, Vrsar 1, Volosca 1, plus 9 moves between houses inside the village itself. Two warnings for whoever reads it next. (1) An opening of this census is ONE table across TWO pages: the left half carries names, rank and birth dates, the right half carries confirmation, marriage, death, the Locus column and vaccination. Reading only the left half loses the origins entirely. (2) The book is ordered by RANK at the front - the 'civilitas' first, then 'rusticus' and 'agricola' - and only settles into house-number order about page 20, and many of the front pages are a HOUSE with an owner named and no household entered under him, because the second column is headed 'Nrus. Inquilinorum' - tenants. A page heading is not a family. ALSO WALKED, and this one is now COMPLETE: on ZM34K-215 the GRACISCE (Gallignana) BAPTISM BOOK 1667-1745, signatura 3.1, is read FRAME BY FRAME end to end - M01069943 to M01070130, 188 frames, title card to the film's KRAJ / END OF ITEM target, every frame, none sampled. Five things the next reader should know before opening it. (1) IT IS TWO REGISTERS, NOT ONE. The title card says MATICNA KNJIGA RODENIH 1667-1745 and MATICNA KNJIGA KRIZMANIH 1690-1694, and the second half is real and substantial: folios 165-171 are a CONFIRMATION ROLL of 16 September 1690 under Bishop Joannes Marcus Rossetti, and folios 174-175 a second of 15 June 1694 under Bishop Petrus Antonius Delle de Hohenberg, numbered to 74. Each line gives child, parent and sponsor. A confirmation roll is the parish's children gathered on ONE DAY before the bishop, so for presence-or-absence questions it is better evidence than a baptism series - and these two are easy to miss because a name-indexed or year-ranged search of 'baptisms 1667-1745' will never reach them. (2) THE BOOK CERTIFIES ITS OWN GAPS. On folio 134 (M01070082), between entries of 17 July and 12 August 1732, the Vicar General Francesco Agostino Corsi - who styles himself on folio 137 'Vic.us Gen.lis Petenensis et Praepositus Pisini', Vicar General of Pedena and Provost of Pazin - left a visitation decree recording that baptisms had been OMITTED from the register through negligence and ordering them recovered and entered without delay. Any nil reported from the baptism half must carry that decree with it. A second visitation mark, 'Revisum in Visitatione &c. die 5. Maij 1745', is drawn across the foot of folio 163 with no complaint attached. (3) IT IS NOT IN CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER, and the decree explains why. Folio 136 carries 1735-1736 while folio 138 carries 1733-1734; at the foot of folio 138 sits a block of six baptisms of April 1732 - January 1733 in a smaller hand under a one-word heading, written in after the fact. A stray baptism of 20 November 1722 sits at the very back, after the confirmation rolls. A SWEEP OF THIS BOOK THAT STEPS BY TWO, OR THAT TRUSTS DATES TO RUN FORWARD, IS NOT A SWEEP. (4) THE FILM'S FRAME COUNT IS NOT THE BOOK'S LEAF COUNT. Three frame-pairs are two exposures of ONE opening, re-shot with a loose slip moved so the text beneath could be read: M01070086/87 (folio 137), M01070093/94 (folio 143), M01070116/117 (folios 164v-165). The second exposure is sometimes the only readable one. (5) THE LAST WRITTEN LEAF IS NOT A REGISTER PAGE. Folio 177 (M01070129) carries the address panel of a folded letter: 'Al Molto Rev.do In Christo Padre ... P. Valeriano da Fiume, Predicatore e Vicario della Venerabile Religione Capucina di Fiume'. A Capuchin letter-cover from Fiume bound into the back of a central-Istrian parish register. Four bishops of Pedena appear in this one volume - von Raunach baptising in person in 1672, Rossetti confirming in 1690, Delle de Hohenberg confirming in 1694, and Josephus Bonifacius Ceccoti baptising in person twice in seven weeks in 1743 - which is worth knowing for a diocese whose own canons swore that no bishop had ever resided in it. Recurring surnames across the whole volume, for anyone deciding whether it is worth their time: Martinich, Milotich, Drusetich, Grach, Baxa, Salamon, Fernasar, Sestan, Poldrugovaz, Dermit, Braissa, Dilizza, Cincopan, Jerbulla, Carlovich, Lupigna, Bertetich, Merletich, Maurovich, Chlaj, Picot, Scuich, Vale, Zotar, Sirol, Lanza, Brosan, Bursich, Copicich, Godenich. NO FAMILYSEARCH WAYPOINT EXISTS for this book: it is a DAPA film, read from a private copy of the reel, not a FamilySearch collection - so it is recorded here by signatura and frame range rather than by a waypoint. ONE MORE THING ABOUT THE GRACISCE BAPTISMS, for anyone who reads them for a surname. From about 1783 (frame M01070190 onward on ZM34K-215) the book stops being narrative Latin and becomes a RULED TABLE, and its columns are: year/month/day, house number, child's name, religion, sex, legitimacy, Pater, Mater, Patrini (Nomen), CONDITIO, Baptizans. Two warnings follow. (1) READING ONE COLUMN IS NOT READING THE BOOK. A sweep of the Pater column of M01070190-M01070226 - about 900 baptisms, 1783 to May 1808 - produced a clean nil for one surname; the PATRINI column of the very same frames then produced about twenty occurrences of it. A surname can sit in Pater, in Mater (written as 'olim' or 'nata' plus the maiden name), in Patrini, or in Conditio, and a question phrased 'did they live here?' names only one of those. (2) THE CONDITIO COLUMN IS SOCIALLY GRADED AND IS EVIDENCE IN ITS OWN RIGHT. It describes the GODPARENTS, not the child, and its values run rustici, villici, agricolae, supani (village headmen), judices, cives (townspeople), nobiles - often with a place attached, as in 'Cives Petinenses' or 'Rustici Lindarenses' or 'Nobiles Pisinenses'. For presence-or-absence questions that column is worth more than the names beside it: it tells you whether a person was of the town or visiting it, and the register withholds a place-epithet from people who are local. The same book's earlier narrative half, by contrast, labels outsiders freely ('Gollagoriciensis', 'Petinensis', 'ex Lindaro'), so a surname that is epithet-tagged before 1783 and bare after it has moved in. The ruled half also carries the parish's own copy of the 1788 Spiritual Visitation certificate at M01070195, and decanal sign-offs - 'Revisus in Visitatione Decanali die 7ma 8bris 1807, Petrus Anicich, Caes. Reg. Parochus et Decanus' at M01070225. The same dean signs the GOLOGORICA registers on 25 June 1808, so one decanal round covered both parishes and a single deanery protocol should account for them together. ALSO NOW OPENED on ZM34K-214, and it had never been read by anyone who recorded the fact: the GOLOGORICA MARRIAGE REGISTER 1770-1789, which sits inside the composite item at M01068953-M01069007 together with baptisms 1770-1781 and deaths 1770-1789 - three registers bound and filmed as one, with NO SIGNATURA on the Pazin paper inventory. The marriages occupy roughly M01068998-M01069006; the item's own KRAJ target is M01069007. Four things about this book are worth knowing before opening it, and the last two are the reason it is worth opening at all. (1) ENTRIES ARE NARRATIVE LATIN TO A FIXED FORMULA, one paragraph per marriage under a centred date heading, with the year carried only by an occasional centred divider rather than on each entry - so a frame can be read without the year being on it, and the year has to be taken from the nearest divider in either direction. (2) IT CARRIES A TRADE COLUMN INSIDE THE PROSE, as 'professionis suae [trade]' for the groom. The overwhelmingly common value is 'Agricola'; anything else on a page of Agricolae is a real statement about a man rather than a formula, and is worth magnifying before transcription because the short trade words differ by one letter (Textor, a weaver, against Tector, a plasterer). (3) IT NAMES THE PRIEST WHO OFFICIATED WITH HIS OFFICE AND HIS PARISH, in the ablative - 'a Reverendissimo Domino Archipresbytero et Parocho [place]ensi [name]' - and that priest is frequently NOT this parish's own. THIS IS THE TRANSFERABLE FINDING: a marriage register names the clergy of neighbouring parishes, so a priest whose own parish's surviving film begins too late to hold him may still be named, in full, in the register of a parish four kilometres away that was filmed from an earlier date. Anyone hunting an eighteenth-century Istrian parish priest should read the neighbours' marriage books before writing to a diocesan archive for a clergy list. (4) IT DISTINGUISHES SAME-NAMED MEN BY PATRONYMIC, as 'quondam [father] filius' for a dead father and 'filio Domini [father]' for a living one - which in a district where a handful of forenames repeat across every household is often the only thing in any register that tells two contemporaries apart. ONE UNSOLVED FEATURE, recorded so the next reader does not assume it: every entry carries a NUMBER IN THE LEFT MARGIN, and on a single opening these run 25, 110, 62, 102, 50, 6, 82, 27, 115, 45, 62, 34, 65 - out of order, with repeats, and too large to be ages. They are not sequential entry numbers and they have not been identified; do not read them as house numbers without testing it. Recurring surnames on the frames read so far: Udovicich, Chrismanich, Defranceschi, Millotich, Besiach, Zabran, Gasparich, Pascoli, Rabar, Bancich, Grah, Grabar, Sestan, Merklin, Rosa, Lucacich, Brosan. NO FAMILYSEARCH WAYPOINT EXISTS for this book either - like the Gracisce baptisms above it is a DAPA film read from a private copy of the reel, so it is recorded by frame range, not by waypoint. ONE MORE THING ON ZM34K-214, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL ITEM ON EITHER REEL FOR THE PRE-1784 GENERATION. The item the Pazin inventory files as 'Gologorica - Umrli - 1646-1806' (M01069199-M01069223) is NOT mainly a death register. It is a PERPETUAL OBIT CALENDAR, and it says so on its own title page at M01069202: 'Catalogus mortuorum in Parochia Gollogoritiae ADULTORUM, ab anno Christianae 1646 usque ad nostra tempora, ex antiquis et recentioribus paginis coactus a me Antonio Ferdinando Mocovrich, Parocho Loci, Anno Domini 1800.' Two months to an opening, the days of the month down each page, and against each day the people who died on that day IN ANY YEAR with the year ruled off at the right. In Italian, not Latin. It runs the full twelve months within about M01069202-M01069221 and was kept up by later hands long after 1806 - the same pages carry 1817, 1819, 1857 and 1887. WHY IT IS WORTH OPENING BEFORE THE REGISTERS. It is a digest, made in 1800, of parish registers running back to 1646 - and for a parish whose pre-1784 death books are not otherwise in the filmed set, it is the only surviving route to them. Sixteen openings read for one surname produced eleven dated entries spanning 1709 to 1804, several naming a filiation ('figlia q. [father]', 'moglie di q. [husband]'), a house number, an age, and occasionally a style such as Signor or Reverendo. For people who otherwise exist only as a year on a family tree it supplies the day, and often the household. THREE WARNINGS, ALL EARNED. (1) 'ADULTORUM' - IT EXCLUDES CHILDREN, so a nil in it is a nil for adults only and a family that buried only infants in the parish is invisible. (2) IT IS A COPY, NOT A WITNESS. For anything before 1800 it is derived from the registers, so where a later register also survives the two are not independent sources and must not be counted as corroboration of each other; what agreement shows is that the compiler copied accurately. (3) IT IS ORDERED BY DAY OF THE YEAR, NOT BY YEAR - you cannot turn to 1773, you must read all twelve months - and the YEAR COLUMN is the faint part of the page. In the entries read, names were crisp while years were blotted, cut at the gutter, or reduced to '170' plus an illegible stroke; every year has to be magnified against its neighbours on the same line, and a year must never be completed from a family tree you are trying to confirm. A first impression at page scale read one year as '177-' which at eight times proved to be '1751' - the difference between confirming a descent and not. Anyone working a central-Istrian parish should check whether its 'deaths' item is actually a book of this kind before planning a page-by-page walk.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Rijeci
providers.what: The Rijeka State Archive — the Kvarner, Fiume's corpus separatum administration, and the Liburnian coast.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Zadru
providers.what: The Zadar State Archive, which holds the Venetian and Austrian registers of Dalmatia — including parishes whose books never went to Split. Its own analytical inventory (HR-DAZD-378, ~2,400 civil-registry books) states the collection's scope explicitly: coastal Dalmatia from Rab in the north to Hvar and Vis in the south. Confirmed by walking the inventory's full parish list: it holds NOTHING for the inland Lika-Senj cluster (Sveti Rok, Lovinac, Gračac, Ričice, Donji Lapac, Gospić) — those parishes are out of scope for this archive, not merely unindexed. The site itself blocks automated/headless browsing (403) but loads normally in an ordinary browser. Its analytical inventory HR-DAZD-378 (Burić and Modrinić, 2014) is now held in data/dazd-378-registers.json: 178 parishes and 1,840 register books with the archive's own signatures, which is what a letter here has to quote.

providers.name: Bayerisches Staatsarchiv Nürnberg
providers.what: Nuremberg, under the Generaldirektion der Staatlichen Archive Bayerns. The state archives of Bavaria publish their holdings and say which services are free.
providers.triageNote: Surveyed 2026-10-09. gda.bayern.de opens with no account asked for; «kostenlos» appears in its own description of services.

providers.name: Bibliothek des Sächsischen Staatsarchivs, Standort Bergarchiv Freiberg
providers.what: The library of the Sächsisches Staatsarchiv at the BERGARCHIV FREIBERG — the mining archive of Saxony, and a reference library rather than a record office. Worth knowing for anyone whose people were miners in the Erzgebirge: the Bergarchiv holds the industry's own records. The library's catalogue is in K10plus, the shared German union catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Surveyed 2026-10-09. archiv.sachsen.de/bibliothek-8493.html opens with no account asked for and links opac.k10plus.de. This row is the library at the Bergarchiv Freiberg standort, not the record holdings themselves.

providers.name: Brandenburgisches Landeshauptarchiv
providers.what: Potsdam. The Brandenburgisches Landeshauptarchiv publishes its holdings and feeds them to Archivportal-D, the German federal archive portal, which is where a cross-state search for a Brandenburg holding should start.
providers.triageNote: Surveyed 2026-10-09. blha.brandenburg.de opens with no account asked for and links www.archivportal-d.de.

providers.name: Evangelisches Landeskirchliches Archiv in Berlin
providers.what: The Kirchliches Archivzentrum in Berlin, for the EKBO. It publishes an Archivsuche over its Bestände and a route for Familienforschung, but the church books themselves are used at the archive; nothing on the site offers them over the web.
providers.triageNote: Surveyed 2026-10-09. landeskirchenarchivberlin.de carries «Bestände · Archivsuche · Kirchenbücher · Benutzung · Wissenschaftliche Forschung · Familienforschung/Genealogie» and links no external register portal — no Archion, no Matricula. Recorded onsite on that absence of any published online route, with the Bestände search noted.

providers.name: Generallandesarchiv Karlsruhe
providers.what: Karlsruhe, which also houses the Dokumentationsstelle Rechtsextremismus. A branch of the Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg, whose finding aids are published together as ONLINE-FINDMITTEL at www2.landesarchiv-bw.de — one search across the Hauptstaatsarchiv Stuttgart, the Generallandesarchiv Karlsruhe and the Staatsarchive, with digitised items attached to the entries that have them.
providers.triageNote: Surveyed 2026-10-09. The branch page opens with no account asked for and names its Bestände; www2.landesarchiv-bw.de/ofs21/suche/ serves «Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg - Online-Findmittel» and answered HTTP 200.

providers.name: Hauptstaatsarchiv Stuttgart

providers.name: Landesarchiv Berlin
providers.what: Landesarchiv Berlin. ITS NAME INDEXES ARE ONLINE AND FREE AND THE REGISTERS THEMSELVES ARE NOT. LABSA (the deep link) is a finding aid to the Namensverzeichnisse -- the name indexes to the birth, marriage and death registers of about 142 Berlin registry offices -- served as whole PDFs, no account, no fee, no viewer. Deaths run year by year to 1994, marriages stop at 1944 and births at 1913, because the protection period is 30 years for a death, 80 for a marriage and 110 for a birth. An index gives a surname, forenames, a day and month, a REGISTER NUMBER and often the confession; the register entry itself, with the address, age, birthplace and informant, is ordered from the archive for a fee. TWO DEFECTS MEASURED IN USE. The search form's three record-type checkboxes DO NOT UNION -- ticking more than one corrupts the result (Schoeneberg returns 61 death volumes alone and 0 with all three ticked), so query one record type per request. And the office name must be exact, with the 'Standesamt ' prefix, double-encoded for the 29 offices whose names carry an umlaut or eszett. ALSO: the PDFs are labelled 'Durchsuchbares PDF durch OCR-Texterkennung' and that label is not a promise about the NAMES -- where a volume is handwritten the OCR has caught the printed headings and almost nothing else, so a volume's text layer must be scored against common surnames before its silence is allowed to mean anything.

providers.name: FamilySearch
providers.what: The largest free collection of record images and indexes in the world. A free account is required, and a minority of images are restricted to Family History Centres and affiliate libraries. TWO TRAPS IN THE CROATIAN HOLDINGS, both verified by use on 2026-10-09 and both capable of producing a confident false nil. (1) THE SAME PARISH SITS IN MORE THAN ONE COLLECTION. Bakar (Buccari) records are indexed under BOTH 'Croatia, Church Books, 1516-1994' (cc=2040054) AND 'Croatia, Delnice Deanery Catholic Church Books, 1571-1926'. A search restricted to 2040054 returns ZERO for records that demonstrably exist in the Delnice Deanery set - a marriage of 1783 at Bakar was found only once the collection filter was dropped. So a nil reported against one Croatian collection is a statement about that collection, never about the parish; and the catalogue's film list for a place may be split across collections that do not cross-reference each other. (2) SEARCH URL PARAMETERS SILENTLY FAIL. Hand-built query strings of the form /search/record/results?q.surname=X&q.anyPlace=Y returned 'Historical Record Search Results (0)' for a record whose own detail page gives exactly that surname and exactly that place string. The same query typed into the search form returns it. Place and collection parameters are the ones observed to fail; a bare q.surname + q.givenName pair did work. THE PRACTICAL RULE: never report a FamilySearch nil from a URL you assembled. Drive the form, and run a known-positive control - an ark id you already hold - through the same path first. An index entry is also a pointer and not a reading: the 1783 marriage above is indexed as two names and a date, and the words 'ex Gollogorizza' in the entry itself - the words that place the groom 130 km away in another crown land and make the record foreign to the Bakar set it sits in - appear nowhere in the index. Open the image before building or dismissing a household on an indexed record. Film and image-group identifiers DO work as stable handles where this collection's viewer carries no wc= waypoint: the Bakar marriage volume is film 005494714, 'Bakar. Religious Marriage Registers 1739-1808', item 1, 226 images, image group M99F-VRM. FULL-RESOLUTION IMAGES CAN BE DOWNLOADED, and it is worth knowing because the viewer's own zoom is a poor substitute for cropping locally. The download control in the image viewer opens a dialog offering 'PDF Record Image with Highlights', 'PDF with No Highlights', 'JPG Only' and 'No Record Image'. Choose JPG Only: it delivers the plate at native scan resolution - a Croatian parish register leaf came down at 5975x4206 - named <filmnumber>_<imagenumber>.jpeg, e.g. 005494714_00172.jpeg, which is a self-describing filename worth keeping. Note that the DeepZoom tiles the viewer itself loads (service/records/storage/deepzoomcloud/dz/v1/apid:<APID>/image_files/<level>/<col>_<row>.jpg) return 401 to an unauthenticated fetch and are blocked by CORS from the www origin, so scraping them is neither possible nor necessary; the download button is the supported route and it works. Resolution matters for more than comfort: a contested initial letter in a surname was settled only by cropping two words at identical magnification from the downloaded file, and the same comparison attempted through the viewer's zoom had been inconclusive.

providers.name: Find a Grave
providers.what: Volunteer-photographed headstones and cemetery indexes, worldwide, with very uneven coverage. Owned by Ancestry but free to read.

providers.name: Findmypast
providers.what: Commercial. The strongest British and Irish collection, including parish registers licensed from diocesan archives and the 1921 census of England and Wales. BT 27 IS NOT ONE FORM AND ITS COLUMNS ARE NOT A CONSTANT. The outward passenger lists were re-drawn across the series, so a field present in one piece proves nothing about another and the era has to be checked before a row is planned around it. Sampled by the Luwinski archive: the 1907 form has NO «last address in the United Kingdom» column at all and buckets ages by nationality instead; the 1937 and 1939 form — printed «P.M. 21», columns (1)–(9) — carries last UK address at (6), country of last permanent residence at (8) and country of intended future permanent residence at (9); a 1951 piece is a typed US military transport manifest filed inside BT 27 with none of the Board of Trade form left. ACROSS EVERY REVISION SEEN, none gives an address in the DESTINATION country — the finest is a country and nothing below it, so «where in Australia did they settle» is not a question this series answers.

providers.name: Fundação Pedro Calmon — Arquivo Público do Estado da Bahia
providers.what: Bahia's state archive, under the foundation that runs it — which is the address that answers. Harvested and its address opened, nothing more: what it holds, what is online and what it costs to look are unchecked here.

providers.name: FreeBMD / FreeREG / FreeCEN
providers.what: Volunteer transcriptions of English and Welsh civil registration, parish registers and censuses. Free, an index only, and not complete — and the incompleteness is the part that bites, because it runs BY QUARTER AND BY DISTRICT and the site is silent about its own gaps. A quarter nobody has transcribed prints no header and no warning, which reads exactly like a quarter in which nobody of that name died. Where a quarter IS transcribed it prints its completeness beside the heading, «(>99%)» and the like. So before quoting an absence from FreeBMD, run a common surname at the same district and quarter: if that returns nothing either, you have found an untranscribed quarter and not an absent person.
providers.triageNote:
MEASURED 7 October 2026 by another session of this project, against two deaths it was hunting: December 1885 deaths absent, with a SMITH control in the Penzance district returning March, June and September 1885 each marked «(>99%)» and no December at all; and Bangor district 1862 deaths absent in all four quarters, with a SMITH control returning zero rows and not one quarter header — which cannot be a real result for a district that size. Recorded here as that session measured it; this session did not re-run those two searches.

VERIFIED HERE 9 October: the search form's «Find» is an UNLABELLED IMAGE BUTTON, <input type="image" name="find" src="/btnFindLg.gif">, as are Count and Reset. The only submits carrying text are «Find Additional» and «View Saved», which belong to the saved-search box and answer with a results-shaped page reading «You must supply the name of a file containing a saved search». A session driving this site by button text will press one of those and conclude FreeBMD returns results furniture with no rows. It does not; it was never asked.

providers.name: FreeREG
providers.what: Volunteer transcriptions of English and Welsh parish registers — baptisms, marriages and burials — free and with no account. An INDEX ONLY: there are no images, and coverage is per-parish and very uneven, so it must be measured before an absence in it means anything. Two measurements from the D'Arcy archive: the Berkeley, Gloucestershire transcript is a thirty-year seventeenth-century fragment, every result falling between 1653 and 1677, so it can test one generation and no more; and for the Bristol non-parochial chapels it holds four registers and 1,551 records in total. A control surname should be run in the same parish before any nil result from it is quoted.
providers.triageNote: Added from the D'Arcy archive, which measured its per-parish coverage twice. No `at`: a volunteer index with no single home.

providers.name: Государственный архив Российской Федерации (GARF)
providers.what: The State Archive of the Russian Federation — the central holder of the Russian and Soviet state record. OPENED 2026-09-29: the site is a reading-room archive, not an image portal. Its own front page is notices about reading room No. 1, delays issuing files from the storage of central administrative, political and state-security bodies, and — dated in the notice itself — the relocation of part of the holdings to Obninsk, closing the federal legislative, executive and judicial fonds entirely from 07.09.2026 to 15.11.2026. Anyone planning a visit or a written request in that window should read those notices first. This is the row Russia did not have: until today the atlas's only Russian source was the GERMAN Federal Archives, tagged for ground the Prussian empire once held — true, and silent about Moscow, the Volga and Siberia.
providers.triageNote: Named from Wikidata; homepage read directly on 2026-09-29 except where the row says otherwise.

providers.name: Gazettes.Africa
providers.what: Digitised government gazettes for 24 African countries, free and full-text searchable. A gazette is where a state prints the things it must announce — naturalisations, estate and insolvency notices, name changes, appointments — so it names ordinary people that no register indexes. The atlas held no gazette of any country before this one.

providers.name: Genealogia w Archiwach
providers.what: A Polish state-archives portal of scanned metrical books — civil registration from the Prussian partition (1874 on), duplicates of Roman Catholic parish registers from before that, and population and registration books from 1837. Separate from Szukaj w Archiwach and run by its own archives. Secondary sources say the scans are free and need no account; NOBODY HERE HAS CONFIRMED THAT, because the site is a Vaadin application that renders nothing without JavaScript, so it is marked unsurveyed rather than taking a blog's word for what it costs. SCANS ARE SERVED BY A LORIS IIIF IMAGE SERVER and can be read in place without downloading: /loris/<id>/<x,y,w,h>/<width>,/0/default.jpg returns an arbitrary region at up to TWICE native resolution, which is enough to settle a difficult hand. info.json returns 403 while image requests succeed, and anything above 2x returns a bare 404. The viewer's own canvas is tainted, so the tile server is the route and screenshots are not. THE PORTAL WILL NOT OPEN A UNIT BY ITS SIGNATURE: a scan's modal id resolves only inside the current search result set, so a neighbouring scan cannot be reached by guessing an id. The route that works is to open any scan's modal, click 'View the document' to expose the unit's own scan list, click Show on the scan wanted, and take the new Loris id from the network log.

An index only — it points you at the scan rather than showing it. — NOTE: the service was answering HTTP 500 on 16 September 2026. Its parent society, genealodzy.pl, is up; the index may be back by the time you read this.

providers.name: Geni
providers.what: One shared world tree. Useful for finding other researchers on the same line; not a record source, and its assertions are only as good as their citations.

providers.name: GenTeam.at
providers.what: Volunteer indexes to the Habsburg lands — Vienna's parish registers, Jewish records, school and guild lists. Free with an account, and it reaches ground the church portals do not.

providers.name: Gloucestershire Archives
providers.what: The county record office for Gloucestershire, holding the parish registers for the Vale of Berkeley and the whole county. IT DOES NOT ANSWER RESEARCH ENQUIRIES — asked in September 2026 for one marriage entry, a Senior Archives Assistant replied «I'm afraid we don't offer any kind of research service» and pointed to two other routes: the Gloucestershire Family History Society, whose volunteers do lookups, and Ancestry, which holds the filmed county registers including marriages and banns to 1938. Free access to those films is available inside a Gloucestershire library or through the society. So: a place to visit or to send a volunteer to, not a place to write to.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Gospiću
providers.what: The state archive for Lika-Senj County (except Senj and Novalja) plus Gračac municipality and Srb from Zadar County — the correct regional archive for Sveti Rok, Lovinac, Donji Lapac, and Gospić parish material, which the Zadar archive explicitly does not hold (see dazd). Its own published holdings list confirms collection HR-DAGS-109, "Zbirka matičnih knjiga" (civil registry books), spanning 1793–1998 — well past where the archive.org scans for this parish cluster stop (1940). No online browsing; access is by written request or in person only. Contact: info@arhiv-gospic.hr, +385 53 560 440, Kanižka 17, 53000 Gospić.

providers.name: Magyar Nemzeti Levéltár (Hungarian National Archives)

providers.name: Žrtve rata 1941–1945 — Muzej žrtava genocida
providers.what: The Museum of Genocide Victims in Belgrade's name-by-name register of people killed in Yugoslavia between 1941 and 1945 — 659,122 records, free and without an account. Searchable by given name, surname, year of birth, the MUNICIPALITY AND PLACE OF RESIDENCE ON 6 APRIL 1941, and by place, year and circumstances of death; each row also carries the parent's name, place of birth and nationality as recorded. That pre-war residence field is what makes it genealogical rather than commemorative: it places a named person in a named village on a fixed date, which is exactly what a register would give you and often the only thing that survives for these years. Counted as an INDEX — it gives structured records, not images of the documents behind them. Scope is the whole of the former Yugoslavia; the countries listed here are the ones seen in the data (Vukovar and Vinkovci, Zavidovići and Lopare, Sremska Mitrovica), so it will also answer for Montenegro and North Macedonia beyond what has been checked here. The interface is Serbian. Read from the site itself on 2026-09-29; access class confirmed by use, not assumed. HOW TO SEARCH IT WITHOUT READING A FAMILY AS ABSENT. The surname field matches EXACTLY, not as a substring: «Franceschi» returns 0 while «Defranceschi» returns 2, so a stem finds nothing and every prefixed form has to be sent as its own query. And the spellings are not interchangeable — they hold DIFFERENT PEOPLE. «Defranceschi» gives two men at Pula and Vodnjan; «Defrančeški» gives a third at Pazin and Gologorica, and neither query returns the other's records. Query the Italian, the Croatian and the diacritic-stripped forms separately and treat the results as additive. Verified by search on 2026-09-29. One more thing worth knowing: the front end races when queries are run back to back, and can paint one query's rows under another's count, so a count is only trustworthy taken one query per page load.
providers.triageNote: Homepage and result grid read directly; 659,122 records reported by the site's own paging.

providers.name: MyHeritage
providers.what: Commercial, with a large tree network and good European newspaper and directory coverage. Search is free; opening a record is not. A LINK CHECKER CANNOT TELL YOU WHETHER A MYHERITAGE CITATION IS ALIVE, measured 2026-10-09 against 428 of them carried into a family archive from a GEDCOM export. Record pages answer an unauthenticated request in one of two ways, and NEITHER IS AN HONEST 200: either a 302 to a door, or HTTP 200 WITH AN 843-BYTE BODY READING «Request unsuccessful. Incapsula incident ID: …». A checker that reads the status code alone therefore reports every one of them as RESOLVING. Any archive auditing its outward citations has to read the body, and should grade these neither alive nor dead.

providers.name: Archives State Agency
providers.what: The State Agency «Архиви» itself — the body that runs the Central State Archives, the military-historical archive at Veliko Tarnovo and all 26 regional state archives. Start here: the digital archive searches every branch from one box. All of Bulgaria's state archives are branches of one body, the State Agency «Архиви», on one site, and the terms are the same for all of them. The free DIGITAL ARCHIVE («ДИГИТАЛЕН АРХИВ») searches each archive separately and returns described items with a full citation — archive > fond > опис > архивна единица > лист — and the image with them. It is a SELECTION, in the hundreds per archive, not a bulk scan of registers. Fond lists and finding aids are published per archive. THE REGISTERS ARE MOSTLY NOT HERE, AND THE REASON IS A LAW: civil registration began on 1 January 1893, the municipality writes the registers and KEEPS THEM FOR 130 YEARS before transferring them to the state archive, so until that term runs out certified copies come from the municipality of birth or residence, not from the archive. Two more doors the agency names itself: it CANNOT certify Bulgarian origin — that is the Executive Agency for Bulgarians Abroad, with citizenship at the Ministry of Justice — and service in the Bulgarian army is checked only by the Държавен военноисторически архив at Veliko Tarnovo.
providers.triageNote: Surveyed 2026-10-09; one survey covers all 28 agency archives, which share a site and a policy. www.archives.government.bg opens with no account asked for. Its ДИГИТАЛЕН АРХИВ form posts to /search.php with an archive id, and a keyword search returns «Показани резултати: N» with thumbnails under /illustrations/ and the citation path «фонд > опис > а.е. > лист»; «Пловдив» in archive 16 returned 86. Each archive page carries Фондове, Фондообразуватели, Архивни справочници, Пътеводители, Списък на фондове and Уникални и особено ценни документи. The «Услуги и използване» page states the 130-year rule: «Актовете по гражданско състояние … се съставят от общината … и се съхраняват в нея 130 години, след което се предават в съответния държавен архив, съгласно чл. 85, ал. 3 от Закона за гражданската регистрация», and that until then «заверени преписи и копия се издават от съответната община». NOT REACHED: the agency documents free access to the digitised Exarchate parish registers «чрез Информационната система на държавните архиви (ИСДА) на адрес: http://isda.archives.government.bg:84/FundSearch.aspx» — isda.archives.government.bg resolves to 212.122.187.196 and timed out on ports 84, 8081, 80 and 443, over http and https, to curl and to a real browser. The same address is behind the site's «Е-УСЛУГИ» link. Recorded as unreachable from here, not as closed.

providers.name: Central State Archives of Bulgaria
providers.what: Централен държавен архив, Sofia — archive id 28, and the one Bulgarian archive with a register series that matters to people outside the country. It holds the ENORIYSKI REGISTRI, the parish registers of the Bulgarian population under the spiritual jurisdiction of the Bulgarian Exarchate in Constantinople across the European Ottoman lands — Eastern (Adrianople) and Western (Aegean) Thrace, and Southern (Aegean), Western (Vardar) and Northern (Pirin) Macedonia. They carry named individuals and count as proof of Bulgarian origin. READ THE DATE CAREFULLY: they were compiled in 1906–1907, so they record only people born before or during those years. The digitised part — fond 246К, inventories 9 and 10 — is FREE, through the state archives' information system ИСДА, which did not answer from here. The CSA also answers enquiries about Bulgarian refugees from Thrace and Macedonia, given full name, place and year of birth, and the settlement they were resettled in. Its own slice of the digital archive answered «снимка» with 70 items.

providers.name: SS. Cyril and Methodius National Library
providers.what: Св. св. Кирил и Методий, the national library in Sofia — and for anyone tracing Bulgarian or Macedonian families BEFORE 1893 this is a better door than the state archives. Its digital library is free «в пълния им обем», and two of its collections are the Ottoman-era equivalents of parish registers: the ДЕФТЕРИ — Ottoman tax and population registers, which list householders village by village — and the СИДЖИЛИ, the kadı court registers. Beside them sit the Oriental documents, Eastern and Slavonic manuscripts, early printed books, and BULGARIAN NEWSPAPERS AND MAGAZINES 1844–1944. The Oriental Collections department alone holds about a million sheets in 342,000 archival units covering the 15th to the early 20th century, in Ottoman Turkish, Arabic and Persian, plus 4,000 manuscript codices and 2,000 volumes of early printed books. There is also the Български исторически архив — personal and institutional papers, with its photographs digitised separately. The catalogue is COBISS, at bg.cobiss.net. This is a legal-deposit library and a separate institution from the State Agency «Архиви»; its terms are its own.
providers.triageNote: Surveyed 2026-10-09; open with no account asked for. nationallibrary.bg answered HTTP 200. The digital library page states «Дигиталните копия в пълния им обем се предоставят на свободен достъп» and lists the collections «Български исторически архив · Български исторически архив – фотографии · Старопечатни книги · Славянски и други ръкописи · Източни ръкописи · Музикална колекция · Периодични издания · Сиджили · Дефтери · Ориенталски старопечатни книги · Ориенталски документи · Оригинална графика · Картографски издания», together with «български вестници и списания от периода 1844-1944 г.». providers.name: National Archives of Australia — RecordSearch
providers.what: Immigration and naturalisation files, service records and alien registration — including the wartime files of European arrivals. NO DEEP LINK IS POSSIBLE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Tried on 2026-09-30: RecordSearch runs on a server session and says so itself — «you are no longer in an active session… a link or bookmark referred to an expired session… RecordSearch requires cookies to be enabled to store a session identifier». A URL carrying a surname cannot be handed to somebody; it lands them on an expiry notice rather than a result. So this row deliberately has no `deepLink` where Cognomix and others do, and anything that wants to send a reader here has to send them to the search screen to type it themselves. Access is genuinely free — the site offers «search as a guest» without an account — which is why it stays `free`.

providers.name: NAAIRS — National Archives of South Africa
providers.what: The South African archives index — estate files above all, which are the backbone of South African genealogy. An index; the file is ordered from the depot. TWO DATABASES SINCE THE 2026 MIGRATION AND ONLY ONE IS COMPLETE: NARSSA's own 'Using the Search Function' page states it is migrating more than 8.3 million entries from the old NAAIRS database to the new one, that the new 'fulltext search' WILL NOT DISPLAY ALL THE RECORDS IN THE SYSTEM, and that 'Search Old NAAIRS database' will provide a more complete search. Both are offered to the public side by side. A NIL FROM THE NEW DATABASE IS THEREFORE NOT A NIL, and any recorded NAAIRS negative should say which database answered and at what address.

providers.name: National Archives of Ireland
providers.what: What survived 1922 and what was rebuilt since — the 1901 and 1911 censuses in full and free, Tithe Applotment books, wills and the census fragments recovered from other collections.

providers.name: National Archives of the Philippines
providers.what: Holds the Spanish-era civil and notarial records and, crucially for Filipino genealogy, the 1849 Catálogo alfabético de apellidos — the decree that assigned surnames by town and is why a Filipino surname often names a province. Answers 403 to a script; opens for a person. Harvested and its address opened, nothing more: what it holds, what is online and what it costs to look are unchecked here.

providers.name: National Archives Catalog (NARA)

providers.name: Nationaal Archief

WieWasWie pools the civil registration indexes of every regional archive and is the usual way in; this is the institution behind the national series — the colonial, military, notarial and VOC material that no index of births and deaths reaches.

providers.name: National Historical Commission of the Philippines

providers.name: Нацыянальны гістарычны архіў Беларусі (NIAB)
providers.what: The National Historical Archives of Belarus, Minsk — the holder of the pre-Soviet Belarusian record. OPENED 2026-09-29, and the front page carries a fact worth more than any catalogue entry: BIOGRAPHICAL RESEARCH REQUESTS FROM PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS WERE SUSPENDED ON 17.09.2026 because of the backlog, and the reading room requires an appointment booked in advance. A letter sent now is not being taken. Check whether that has lifted before planning around it. Until today Belarus's only source in this atlas was POLAND's archive portal, correct for the old Kresy Wschodnie and silent on Minsk and everything east.
providers.triageNote: Named from Wikidata; homepage read directly on 2026-09-29 except where the row says otherwise.

providers.name: National Records of Scotland

providers.name: NSK digitalna — Nacionalna i sveučilišna knjižnica
providers.what: The National and University Library in Zagreb's digital portal: Croatian newspapers and periodicals, browsable and free. ANNO covers this ground in German for the Habsburg years; this is the Croatian-language press, which is where a family is named in its own language. The oldest run — Stare hrvatske novine — is served from dnc.nsk.hr over http, which the portal links to; the portal itself is https and is the entry point recorded here. The newspaper archive itself is listed separately as nsk-stare-novine.

providers.name: Stare hrvatske novine (NSK)
providers.what: Stare hrvatske novine — the National and University Library in Zagreb's digitised Croatian newspaper runs, the oldest of them, browsable by title and year. Its sibling row nsk-digitalna is the same library's wider digital portal and links here; this is the newspaper archive itself, listed separately because it is served from its own host and is what a reader is told to open. Worked by the Defranceski archive for «Galeb» and «Kvarner», the two Bakar papers. A newspaper is not a register, but it dates a family to a town when no register survives. Access not yet surveyed.
providers.triageNote: Added from the family research archives, which record work actually done here. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Raduraksti — Latvian State Historical Archives

providers.name: Mi Registro Civil
providers.what: Mexico's Plataforma Nacional del Registro Civil. OPENED 2026-09-29, AND IT IS NOT A GENEALOGICAL SOURCE — worth saying plainly, because its name promises one. It is a SERVICES portal: you pick one of the 32 entidades from a dropdown (Aguascalientes through Zacatecas, plus EXTRANJERO) and it shows the trámites that state offers — ordering a certified copy of a civil record, and checking the status of a request you already made. There is no historical search, no index to browse and no images. Mexican civil registration is administered per state, and this is the front door to thirty-two separate state offices rather than a national record set. Filed as `catalogue` because that is the nearest true class — the paper is not photographed and must be asked for — though even a catalogue is more than it offers.
providers.triageNote: Homepage opened and its own form read on 2026-09-29

providers.triageNote: Unreachable 2026-10-09. stadtarchiv.reutlingen.de returned nothing to curl — no status, no bytes. Row stays unsurveyed.

providers.name: Szukaj w Archiwach
providers.what: The Polish state archives' scans, free and without an account. Covers ground now in Ukraine, Belarus and Lithuania as well as Poland.

providers.name: Torre do Tombo / Digitarq
providers.what: The Portuguese national archive's scans, free. District archives publish parish registers through the same system.

providers.name: Trove
providers.what: The National Library of Australia's newspaper and gazette archive. Free and full-text. Most titles stop at 1954 for copyright, which is the usual rule of thumb — BUT TWO EXCEPTIONS REACH MUCH LATER AND ARE EASY TO MISS: THE CANBERRA TIMES IS DIGITISED 1926-1995, and the COMMONWEALTH OF AUSTRALIA GAZETTE 1901-1973, whose naturalisation and citizenship lists carry name, street address and date. Those two make Trove usable for post-war arrivals that the 1954 rule would rule out. NOTE THAT THE SEARCH NORMALISES SPELLING — two different spellings of one surname can return an identical result set — SO TROVE CANNOT BE USED AS A SPELLING TEST. The v3 API needs an X-API-KEY header and does not serve article text at ordinary key level; the public article page carries the OCR.

providers.name: WieWasWie / Open Archieven
providers.what: The Dutch civil registration indexes, pooled from every regional archive. Free, and unusually complete.

providers.name: WikiTree
providers.what: A free, single shared tree with an unusually strong sourcing culture. Not a record source.

providers.name: Yad Vashem — Central Database of Shoah Victims' Names
providers.what: Names and testimony pages for victims of the Shoah, free.

providers.name: Cognomix — Mappe dei cognomi italiani
providers.what:
Cognomix — where an Italian surname is, by region. OPENED 2026-09-29 on /mappe-dei-cognomi-italiani/FORNASAR, which reports «circa 25 famiglie Fornasar in Italia» and breaks it down: Piemonte 11, Friuli V.G. 8, Veneto 4, Liguria 1, Puglia 1, drawn on a Leaflet map of Italy. Free, no account, and the URL takes the surname uppercased, so a page can be linked to directly.
WHAT IT COUNTS IS FAMILIES TODAY, NOT RECORDS. This is the Italian equivalent of the national-register rows this atlas already holds for Croatia, Slovenia and France — «how many people of that name a state counted», the closest thing to «where the name is now» — and the same caveat applies twice over: it says nothing about where a family was in 1780, and a small number tells you as much about the source as about the name. It is an INDEX, not images: there is no register behind it to open.
The page carries heavy third-party advertising, which is worth knowing before sending somebody there but says nothing about the data.
providers.triageNote: Opened on a real surname page (FORNASAR) on 2026-09-29; the distribution and its per-region counts read directly off the page.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Dubrovniku
providers.what: The state archive of Dubrovnik, in the Sponza palace, holding the records of the Republic of Ragusa, which was its own state until 1808 and kept its own chancery. IMPORTANT, AND THE REASON THIS ROW EXISTS: it NO LONGER HOLDS THE PARISH REGISTERS. A senior archivist there wrote on 28 September 2026 that «Državni arhiv u Dubrovniku predao je sve matične knjige Biskupskom ordinarijatu u Dubrovniku» — all the matične knjige have gone to the Diocesan Ordinariate — and referred the enquiry on. So a register question addressed here is answered with a redirect, and the Republic's own pre-1808 fonds is what this institution is still for.
providers.triageNote: Added from a family archive after a reply from the archive itself. Access class not surveyed. NOTE the atlas's existing asd-ragusa is the Archivio di Stato di RAGUSA IN SICILY, on Antenati — not this. Ragusa is the Italian name of Dubrovnik and the two are a standing trap.

providers.name: Arhiv Dubrovačke biskupije (Biskupski ordinarijat)
providers.what: The diocesan archive of Dubrovnik, and SINCE THE TRANSFER THE HOLDER OF THE CITY'S PARISH REGISTERS: the state archive states it handed over all the matične knjige and gives this as the address for them. Contact arhiv@db.hr, telephone 020 324 913, both as given by the state archive on 28 September 2026. Nothing has been asked of it yet, and no statement about what it holds volume by volume, what it charges, or whether it answers by email, is made here — only that it is where the registers went.
providers.triageNote: Recorded ONLY on the state archive's own referral, not from the diocese. Its holdings, access and whether it replies are all unsurveyed. Wikidata id not looked up.

providers.name: HDA — Pretraga matičnih knjiga (HR-HDA-1448)
providers.what: The Croatian State Archives' own searchable index of HR-HDA-1448, «Zbirka dopunskih mikrofilmova matičnih knjiga i popisa obitelji» — registers of ALL confessions across Croatia, plus Bosnian Catholics, from the mid-16th to the first half of the 20th century, microfilmed from originals held in state archives, church archives, parish offices, registry offices and monasteries. This answers «is this parish filmed at all» in one query, which arhinet's own row cannot: three drop-downs (parish/regiment, confession, type), then Pretraži. A row gives the period, PRIJEPIS when it is a transcript rather than the original, the holding institution, the signatura svitka (e.g. ZM-34C/681), the topografska oznaka (e.g. M-1278) and Digitalni oblik Da/Ne. Types: R births, V marriages, U deaths, S status animarum, Z confirmations, O anniversarii, I index. To order: info@arhiv.hr with place, type, period, signatura and topografska oznaka; consulted in the HDA reading room in Zagreb, max ten units a day. TWO TRAPS. First, the place box is a Telerik combo on an ASP.NET page: setting it FROM SCRIPT changes only what it displays and never commits to the server, so the search runs on an empty place and returns «Nema zapisa za pregled» — identical to a real nil. On 2026-09-29 that manufactured nine false negatives in one sitting, caught only by re-running a known-positive place as a control and watching it come back empty too. Always run that control. Second, the site itself warns that one settlement may be listed under several name forms — CRIKVENICA has four — so check every variant before calling a place absent.
providers.triageNote: Added from a family archive after using it to settle whether one Lika parish was filmed. Free and needs no login; access class 'index' because it indexes holdings rather than serving images — nothing in HR-HDA-1448 was found digitised for the parish tested.

providers.name: HR-HDA-883 — Zbirka matičnih knjiga (Hrvatski državni arhiv)
providers.what: The Croatian State Archives' own collection of ORIGINAL parish registers — distinct from HR-HDA-1448, which is microfilm of registers held elsewhere, and from the register search at provider hda-mk-search, which indexes 1448 and not this. Covers parishes of the Zagreb archdiocese, the Đakovo-Srijem and SENJ-MODRUŠ dioceses, Orthodox parishes of the Gornji Karlovac eparchy, and others. A published inventory lists it parish by parish with date ranges: Angelika Milić, «Zbirka matičnih knjiga u Hrvatskom državnom arhivu», Arhivski vjesnik 60 (2017), 251-311, https://hrcak.srce.hr/194831. A machine-readable extract of those holdings exists — 2,503 volumes across 357 parishes, 1585-1947, as parish/confession/type/date-range — held by the Defranceschi family archive and available on request. IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT COMMITTED HERE: this atlas's own licence gate is right that a dataset dropped into data/ becomes something the atlas must publish and disclose on /data/, and whether to take on a source with no stated publisher licence is the atlas's decision, not a contributing archive's. THE DATE CUT IS THE IMPORTANT THING AND IT IS NOT ARBITRARY: a decision of the NRH Ministry of the Interior of 13 May 1949 required every register with entries UP TO 1860 to be handed to the competent archive, while those from 1860 onward stayed with the state registry offices that needed them in daily work. So a parish that appears here ending in 1858 has not stopped keeping records — anything after 1860 is simply somewhere else, normally the matični ured or the parish. That single rule explains a great many apparent gaps across Croatia.
providers.triageNote: Added from a family archive. access 'onsite': the originals are consulted on paper in the HDA reading room; no online images are known to this row. An extract of the printed inventory exists but is NOT committed here — see the description. It is a conservative parse and undercounts: it reads only «MKR 1789.–1833.» forms, so single-year and index entries are missing, about 2,503 of 3,017 candidate lines.

providers.name: Queensland State Archives
providers.what: Queensland's state archive. ArchivesSearch is an item-level catalogue, free and open, covering court, lands, immigration, police and school records. VERIFIED IN USE: the series Supreme Court (Northern) Ecclesiastical Files (Wills) S6220 alone holds 15,707 items, named per person, each marked open access. Catalogue only — the files themselves are paper and must be ordered or viewed on site; a catalogue entry gives the name, a year and an item ID and nothing more. A usable JSON endpoint exists at /api/fetch?uri=/repositories/2/archival_objects/<id>, which returns the full record including its series and preferred citation. The /api/search endpoint is live but its free-text parameter was not established: type[] is accepted and every text parameter tried was rejected. Trove indexes a subset of these item records, so they can also be reached from there.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Mazza Family archive after reading item records through both the /api/fetch endpoint and Trove. Access class is catalogue on the evidence of the catalogue itself; what an ordinary visitor pays to ORDER a file has not been surveyed.

providers.name: City of Cape Town — City Parks, cemeteries and burial registers
providers.what: The municipality that HOLDS THE ORIGINAL burial registers for about forty Cape Town cemeteries, Maitland (Woltemade) among them — FamilySearch's Cape cemetery collection names it as the location of the originals. NO ONLINE RECORD SEARCH WAS FOUND: the cemetery pages advertise burials, cremations, exhumations and grave reservations, and list telephone numbers, with nothing said about historical registers or genealogy enquiries. So this is a WRITE-OR-TELEPHONE source, not a searchable one. WHAT IS ONLINE INSTEAD is FamilySearch collection 2790463, 'South Africa, Cape, Cemetery Records 1872-2011', about 41,900 images of these same registers, digitised from the City's own Cape Metro Cemetery Records — and REDACTED: the cause-of-death column is blacked out, so the City's own copy holds something the digitisation does not.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Lerena archive, which read two openings of the Maitland Road Cemetery Record of Interments on 8 October 2026. ACCESS CLASS STILL NEEDS A PERSON: the homepage was fetched and the FamilySearch collection page read, and nothing was ordered, telephoned or paid for, so 'unsurveyed' is the honest class. The Wikidata id is the metropolitan municipality, which is the body that holds the records; there is no separate item for City Parks.

providers.name: Llyfrgell Genedlaethol Cymru / National Library of Wales
providers.what: Aberystwyth. The legal deposit library for Wales. Its own navigation names four digital collections — TITHE MAPS, NEWSPAPERS, JOURNALS and the CATALOGUE. The newspaper service is WELSH NEWSPAPERS ONLINE at newspapers.library.wales, advertised as free and covering 1804–1919, which is the run that matters for Welsh families whose notices are otherwise only on subscription sites. NOT YET SURVEYED: what an ordinary visitor can actually retrieve was not established on this visit, because the newspaper service did not open (see the triage note). The main site at library.wales is open and needs no account to browse.
providers.triageNote: Added from the D'Arcy archive, 2026-10-09, while looking for a free copy of a Caernarvon & Denbigh Herald obituary of 1843. A NATIONAL LIBRARY THE ATLAS DID NOT LIST: before this row, the only providers covering Wales were Findmypast and the GRO, both paid. REACHED: www.library.wales loaded normally. NOT REACHED: newspapers.library.wales returned a Cloudflare «Performing security verification» interstitial that did not clear in about forty seconds, on a search URL and again on the bare homepage. It was NOT worked around. That is one browser on one day and is not an access class — the interstitial clears for most visitors — so access stays «unsurveyed» until somebody gets in and says what is free.

providers.name: The Gazette (London, Edinburgh and Belfast)
providers.what: The official journal of record of the United Kingdom, free and full-text searchable back to 1665, with no account. THREE EDITIONS — London, Edinburgh and Belfast — and the same notice is frequently printed in two of them days apart, which is a free second reading of the SAME TEXT UNDER DIFFERENT OCR. A gazette names ordinary people no register indexes: army and navy commissions and every promotion, colonial and civil appointments, insolvencies and bankruptcies, naturalisations, changes of name, partnerships dissolved, probate and estate notices. Verified 2026-10-09 by reconstructing a career from Ensign in 1837 to the government of a colony in 1859 out of ten notices, for a man previously known only from two index entries.
providers.triageNote: Added from the D'Arcy archive, 2026-10-09. TWO OPERATIONAL FACTS, BOTH MEASURED. (1) THE OCR MANGLES NAMES AND THE SEARCH IS OVER THE OCR: one man appears as «Qeorge», «Greorge» and «D'Aroy» across his own notices, so a surname search misses most of a career and the thing to search is whichever token is least corruptible — an unusual middle name beat both his forename and his surname. (2) A MULTI-WORD QUERY COMBINED WITH A DATE RANGE RETURNS HTTP 500 and redirects to a sign-in page, which looks like a paywall and is not one; a single token with a date range, or a quoted phrase without one, both work. An apostrophe in the query does the same.
